I think either the Brother or Epson product lines are the only decent remaining consumer side printers/scanners you can buy.

Also (separate issue), I am on Antergos Linux. No matter the distro, wireless printing is a constant pain in the ass. What I mean is that printers constantly get forgotten or set to 'not-enabled'.

Color printing is not important to me. Scanning and printing is. I would prefer to just plug it directly in to my router and leave wireless off or not even have wireless. At this point of anger I am happy to crawl under the house and run wires.

Don't try to use a printer underwater.

More seriously :

  1. Don't buy a all in one piece of crap. Better buy a printer and a scanner separately.

  2. Choose your printer according to the price of a refill : You'll end up saving money even if the printer itself is far more expensive.

  3. Check how well supported your chosen devices are on Linux: Scanners and Printers

  4. Write down any first time set up needs for your devices : You won't forget to install a needed firmware file that way. ( the Mustek 1248UB scanner works great on Linux but I tend to forget to do that on a new installation )

Also : Choose wisely, choose Laser.

I work in the reman/refill business, so if I can amend your number 2 point just a bit. Go by the unit value, or price per page of the consumables. HP61 inkjet carts might be inexpensive, but they're basically trial size. Price per mL is outrageous, something like $3.75

Printers are my job. Since it sounds like you're fine with an laser, there are two options. Two. Out of all of those manufacturers, TWO don't produce unadulterated shit.

Your decent budget option is Brother. Solid machines, not much to fuck up, few problems, etc. Inexpensive but good, easy to find supplies for, wide range of options to suit what your needs are in terms of volume or wireless, fax, etc. My Brother printer has worked right fine with various Linux distros.

Your built like a fucking tank but expensive option is Oki. Every emissions place around me has an Oki because you could hit one with your car, and it would be fine, but you'd have to buy a new car. There's a gas station up the road that uses one, and they had it crammed in a precarious place where it was getting shit spilled on it, kicked by accident, the area trapped heat, you name it, and the thing lasted them 10 years.

After as long as I've worked in this business, those are the only two laser printer manufacturers I'd even consider. I'd personally lean on Brother due to costs and ease of getting supplies.

The biggest question is volume. If you've got a home business, you're a college student, or something similar, a model that takes the TN-660 cartridge should be fine. They're about $75 retail OEM, $40 at my store, and likely under $15 on eBay. Those are rated at "2600" pages, so realistically you'll get about 1200-1600 out of them. You'll need to replace the drum unit on a Brother after roughly four cartridges. Those are pricey, but you're not paying each time for drums that are built into the cartridge that don't necessarily need to be replaced with HP or Canon (which are just rebranded HP's) .
